title: What makes us late
paragraphs: As the saying goes, ‘time waits for no man’. Time is always against us, and we just can’t stop it. Maybe that’s why some of us are always running late for appointments. But if timekeeping is not what you’re good at, don’t stress. There might be a good reason for your lack of punctuality.

People’s attitudes to being on time vary. Some clock-watch and make sure they’re bang on time for a meeting. It is, after all, rude to be late, and if you can make it on time, why can’t everyone else? But if, like me, you want to make every second count, you might try to squeeze as much as you can into the time you have available. However, when your schedule doesn’t run to plan, your punctuality inevitably slips.

People who lack promptness have been described as ‘time benders’. Author Grace Pacie told the BBC that “they’re the people who don’t want to be late, but they have a strange resistance to being early, and they don’t allow enough time.” They assume their journey to an appointment will always go smoothly, and the train will always be on time!

Perceptions of unpunctual people are almost always negative – even if sometimes wrong. Writing for the BBC, Laura Clarke says: “Being consistently late might not be your fault. It could be your type. The punctually-challenged often share personality characteristics, such as optimism, low levels of self-control, anxiety, or a penchant for thrill-seeking, experts say. It is also possible people are late so not to be conspicuous and to avoid the anxious wait for others to turn up.

Maybe us latecomers should make more of an effort and follow the advice I heard to not ‘try’ to be on time but ‘decide’ to be on time. But I know if a meeting or a deadline really matters, then I’ll be there. Otherwise relax, even if others are cursing you!

vocabulary.term: time waits for no man 岁月不待人
vocabulary.entry: time waits for no man 岁月不待人
vocabulary.example: My grandfather always reminds me that time waits for no man.
vocabulary.translation: 爷爷总是提醒我，岁月不待人。

vocabulary.entry: run late 迟到；晚点
vocabulary.example: We will run late if we don't leave in five minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 如果五分钟内还不走，我们就要迟到了。

vocabulary.entry: appointment /əˈpɔɪntmənt/ n. 约会；预约
vocabulary.example: I have a dental appointment tomorrow morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我明天上午有个牙科预约。

vocabulary.entry: timekeeping /ˈtaɪmkiːpɪŋ/ n. 守时；计时
vocabulary.example: Her timekeeping is excellent; she is never late for work.
vocabulary.translation: 她非常守时，上班从不迟到。

vocabulary.entry: punctuality /ˌpʌŋktʃuˈæləti/ n. 准时；守时
vocabulary.example: Punctuality is highly valued in business meetings.
vocabulary.translation: 商务会议中，守时是非常重要的品质。

vocabulary.entry: clock-watch /ˈklɒk wɒtʃ/ v. 盯着时钟看；盼下班
vocabulary.example: The students began to clock-watch as the end of class approached.
vocabulary.translation: 下课时间快到，学生们开始盯着时钟看。

vocabulary.term: bang on time 准时；分秒不差
vocabulary.entry: bang on time 准时；分秒不差
vocabulary.example: The conference started bang on time at 9 a.m.
vocabulary.translation: 会议上午九点准时开始。

vocabulary.term: make every second count 让每一秒都有意义；珍惜时间
vocabulary.entry: make every second count 让每一秒都有意义；珍惜时间
vocabulary.example: During the exam, you should make every second count.
vocabulary.translation: 考试时，你要珍惜每一分每一秒。

vocabulary.entry: squeeze /skwiːz/ v. 挤入；塞进
vocabulary.example: She managed to squeeze all her belongings into a small suitcase.
vocabulary.translation: 她设法把所有东西都塞进了一个小手提箱里。

vocabulary.entry: available /əˈveɪləbl/ adj. 可用的；可支配的
vocabulary.example: Do you have any time available tomorrow afternoon?
vocabulary.translation: 你明天下午有空吗？

vocabulary.entry: schedule /ˈʃedjuːl/ n. 日程安排；计划表
vocabulary.example: I need to check my schedule before agreeing to the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 我得先看看日程安排，再决定要不要参加这个会议。

vocabulary.term: run to plan 按计划进行
vocabulary.entry: run to plan 按计划进行
vocabulary.example: The wedding ran to plan despite the bad weather.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管天气不好，婚礼还是按计划顺利进行了。

vocabulary.entry: inevitably /ɪnˈevɪtəbli/ adv. 不可避免地；必然地
vocabulary.example: If you keep working like this, you will inevitably feel tired.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你一直这样工作，难免会感到疲惫。

vocabulary.entry: promptness /ˈprɒmptnəs/ n. 迅速；敏捷
vocabulary.example: The promptness of his response impressed the manager.
vocabulary.translation: 他的迅速回应给经理留下了深刻印象。

vocabulary.entry: time bender /ˈtaɪm bendə/ n. 时间拖延者
vocabulary.example: My brother is a real time bender who always arrives five minutes late.
vocabulary.translation: 我哥哥是个十足的时间拖延者，每次都迟到五分钟。

vocabulary.entry: resistance /rɪˈzɪstəns/ n. 抗拒；抵触
vocabulary.example: She showed great resistance to changing her daily routine.
vocabulary.translation: 她非常抗拒改变自己的日常作息。

vocabulary.entry: assume /əˈsjuːm/ v. 假定；想当然认为
vocabulary.example: I assume you have read the report I sent last week.
vocabulary.translation: 我以为你已经看过我上周发的报告了。

vocabulary.entry: journey /ˈdʒɜːni/ n. 行程；旅程
vocabulary.example: The journey from my home to the office takes about 30 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 从我家到办公室的路程大概需要30分钟。

vocabulary.entry: perception /pəˈsepʃn/ n. 看法；认知
vocabulary.example: Public perception of the new policy has changed over time.
vocabulary.translation: 公众对这项新政策的看法随着时间发生了改变。

vocabulary.entry: consistently /kənˈsɪstəntli/ adv. 一贯地；始终如一地
vocabulary.example: The team has consistently won matches this season.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍本赛季的比赛一直连胜。

vocabulary.entry: punctually-challenged /ˌpʌŋktʃuəli ˈtʃælɪndʒd/ adj. 不守时的
vocabulary.example: Punctually-challenged people often struggle with meeting deadlines.
vocabulary.translation: 不守时的人通常很难按时完成任务。

vocabulary.entry: self-control /ˌself kənˈtrəʊl/ n. 自控力；自制力
vocabulary.example: It takes a lot of self-control to resist eating junk food.
vocabulary.translation: 抵制垃圾食品需要很强的自控力。

vocabulary.entry: penchant /ˈpentʃənt/ n. 嗜好；偏爱
vocabulary.example: She has a penchant for collecting vintage postcards.
vocabulary.translation: 她酷爱收集复古明信片。

vocabulary.entry: conspicuous /kənˈspɪkjuəs/ adj. 显眼的；引人注目的
vocabulary.example: He felt conspicuous in his bright red jacket at the formal event.
vocabulary.translation: 在这场正式活动上，他穿着鲜红色夹克，显得格外惹眼。

vocabulary.entry: latecomer /ˈleɪtkʌmə/ n. 迟到者
vocabulary.example: The teacher asked the latecomer to explain his reason for being late.
vocabulary.translation: 老师让迟到的学生解释自己迟到的原因。

sentences.english: As the saying goes, ‘time waits for no man’.
Time is always against us, and we just can’t stop it.
sentences.chinese: 时间总在与我们作对，而我们对此束手无策。

sentences.english: Maybe that’s why some of us are always running late for appointments.
sentences.chinese: 或许这就是有些人赴约总迟到的原因。

sentences.english: But if timekeeping is not what you’re good at, don’t stress. There might be a good reason for your lack of punctuality.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你不擅长守时，不必焦虑，你缺乏准时性或许是有充分理由的。

sentences.english: People’s attitudes to being on time vary.
sentences.chinese: 人们对待守时的态度各不相同。

sentences.english: Some clock-watch and make sure they’re bang on time for a meeting.
sentences.chinese: 有些人总盯着时钟，确保开会准时到场。

sentences.english: It is, after all, rude to be late, and if you can make it on time, why can’t everyone else?
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，迟到是不礼貌的行为，既然你能准时，其他人为什么不能呢？

sentences.english: But if, like me, you want to make every second count, you might try to squeeze as much as you can into the time you have available.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你和我一样，想让每一秒都过得有意义，就可能会试图在有限的时间里塞进尽可能多的事情。

sentences.english: However, when your schedule doesn’t run to plan, your punctuality inevitably slips.
sentences.chinese: 然而，当你的日程安排未能按计划进行时，你就难免会变得不守时。

sentences.english: People who lack promptness have been described as ‘time benders’.
sentences.chinese: 那些做事拖沓的人被称为“时间拖延者”。

sentences.english: Author Grace Pacie told the BBC that “they’re the people who don’t want to be late, but they have a strange resistance to being early, and they don’t allow enough time.”
sentences.chinese: 作家格雷丝·帕西在接受BBC采访时表示：“这类人其实不想迟到，但他们就是莫名抗拒早到，而且预留的出行时间总是不够。”

sentences.english: They assume their journey to an appointment will always go smoothly, and the train will always be on time!
sentences.chinese: 他们想当然地认为，赴约路上一定会一帆风顺，火车也总会准点到站。

sentences.english: Perceptions of unpunctual people are almost always negative – even if sometimes wrong.
sentences.chinese: 人们对不守时者的看法几乎都是负面的——即便有时这种看法并不准确。

sentences.english: Writing for the BBC, Laura Clarke says: “Being consistently late might not be your fault. It could be your type.
sentences.chinese: 劳拉·克拉克在为BBC撰写的文章中称：“总是迟到或许不是你的错，可能是性格使然。

sentences.english: The punctually-challenged often share personality characteristics, such as optimism, low levels of self-control, anxiety, or a penchant for thrill-seeking, experts say.
sentences.chinese: 专家表示，不守时的人往往有着相似的性格特质，比如乐观、自控力差、容易焦虑或是喜欢寻求刺激。

sentences.english: It is also possible people are late so not to be conspicuous and to avoid the anxious wait for others to turn up.
sentences.chinese: 还有一种可能是，人们迟到是为了避免过于引人注目，同时也不想焦灼地等待他人到来。

sentences.english: Maybe us latecomers should make more of an effort and follow the advice I heard to not ‘try’ to be on time but ‘decide’ to be on time.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们这些迟到星人应该再努努力，遵循我听过的一条建议：不要“试着”准时，而是“下定决心”准时。

sentences.english: But I know if a meeting or a deadline really matters, then I’ll be there.
sentences.chinese: 不过我心里清楚，要是某个会议或截止日期真的很重要，我肯定会准时到场。

sentences.english: Otherwise relax, even if others are cursing you!
sentences.chinese: 至于其他情况，就放宽心吧，即便别人在心里咒骂你也没关系！
